skill.name: Plan
skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For behavior changes, identify the underlying cause, governing concept or invariant, and existing owner before listing edits. Prefer strengthening an existing concept; introduce one only when it clarifies the behavior and reduces special cases. Do not change repository files. 

### Guidance

- Thrashing is a real danger with AI agents. To mitigate this, consider if the Goal is merely a symptom of a missing or misused concept in the target app architecture. Feel free to explore other Goals to determine if they have additional insights into this question.
- Over- or under-specificity can also cause undesirable implementation outcomes. Ensure that the plan has the information it needs for effective implementation, but not unnecessary details.
- Always use plain language.

### Format

Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

Example:
Task #1 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
Task #2 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
(etc.)

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.

default-plan.summary:
Planning method: review the retained implementation against the requested behavior, then correct only verified gaps.

Cause and governing invariant: Controls previously combined operating settings with Skill execution and Site access. These already have separate feature owners. The shell should provide consistent navigation and interactions; Skills and Knowledge Hub should continue owning their lists, creation flows, and actions. Strengthen that existing separation without introducing another menu framework or backend concept.

Task #1 - Preserve and assess the retained implementation. Start from f3945f54 and compare it with the requirements below. Treat the earlier implementation report as historical evidence, not current verification; do not recreate completed work.

Task #2 - Confirm shell organization in index.html. Right-aligned controls must appear as Skills, Sites, Settings, New Goal. Rename the visible Controls label and related accessibility text to Settings. Keep Skill and Site lists exclusively in their respective dropdowns, while retaining existing context selectors, settings actions, and New Goal companion actions.

Task #3 - Verify feature-owned actions in settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js. Skills must list applicable enabled Custom Skills, followed by a separator, New Skill, and Manage Skills. Sites must list the attached application's sites, followed by a separator, New Site, and Manage Sites. Reuse existing creation modals, Skill parameter preflight and agent launch, management routes, and draft/published Site links. Keep creation and management available when lists are empty or fail to load. Confirm opening, relevant mutations, and context changes refresh lists without stale responses replacing current entries.

Task #4 - Validate shared interactions and layout in common.js and base.css. Reuse existing menu summaries, rows, icons, spacing, and theme styles. Verify one open menu at a time, dismissal after actions and outside clicks, keyboard activation, and Escape focus restoration. Check long lists at 1440, 800, and 375 pixels in both themes, including panel bounds, scrolling, and access to bottom actions. Correct shared behavior in its existing owner if a defect is demonstrated.

Task #5 - Check documentation consistency. Retain the candidate's updates to browser navigation intent, Skills, Knowledge Hub, and related Guide/onboarding references. Runtime intent still describes the former Controls arrangement; this Round intentionally updates that navigation while preserving the documented capability semantics.

Task #6 - Verify the final candidate. Run the topbar navigation, Knowledge Hub, screen-render, and Controls Node-selector JavaScript suites with Chromium available for browser checks; require zero browser skips. Run the Rust static-surface navigation tests and git diff --check. Ensure coverage includes both draft and published Site opening, creation and management destinations, Skill launch, context refresh races, and unchanged Settings controls. Inspect desktop and narrow layouts visually. Report exact results and any limitations for Quality; add focused regression coverage only for uncovered requirements or demonstrated defects.

No repository files or Goal state were changed during planning.
